paragraph: Mahwah's single-family market is genuinely competitive right now. Sixty-three sales over six months at a median of $1,050,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.027, 60 percent closing above asking, and a median of 18 days on market. Sellers are dictating terms on the well-presented homes. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with two full baths, and while sales ranged from $55,000 up to $2,600,000, the median is the number to anchor on. Condos and townhouses are the larger tier by volume with 102 sales at a median of $513,750, mostly two-bedroom, two-bath units split roughly two-thirds condo to one-third townhouse, moving in 14 days with 75 percent going over ask. Both tiers show medians easing in June and July while closing volume climbed to its highest months of the period, which reads as a mix shift toward smaller and entry-level product rather than values dropping. If Mahwah follows the usual seasonal arc, expect volume to taper modestly through fall and thin out in deep winter. If you're weighing the two tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat, since both are hot. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a condo or townhouse.
